After analyzing the retrieved healthcare Q&A matches, we can synthesize the following clear and concise answer to your question:

The American Academy of Ophthalmology (AAO) suggests that both advanced surface ablation and sub-Bowman's keratomileusis are improvements in excimer laser keratorefractive surgery compared to conventional LASIK or PRK, with regard to maintaining corneal biomechanics. However, most of the disadvantages caused by wound healing issues remain.

This means that while these two procedures may have some benefits, they are not without their drawbacks and should be considered on a case-by-case basis when evaluating the best course of treatment for each individual patient.
